results.content: The Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC), the branch of the Federal Reserve System responsible for national monetary policy, meets eight times per year, or about every six weeks. The FOMC has two main goals: to keep prices stable and keep employment rates high. Its decision to raise, lower or keep rates the same depends on data related to those two goals. At each meeting, the committee analyzes that data, looking at trends related to inflation, the labor market and broader economic growth.
